summary: This note describes the United States Mint's First Spouse Program, which began in 2007 and issues half-ounce $10 gold coins engraved with portraits of the First Ladies on the obverse. When a President served without a spouse, the coin instead shows an image of Liberty from a circulating coin of that era on the obverse and a reverse emblematic of that President's life. The note says this applies to the coins for Thomas Jefferson, Andrew Jackson, Martin Van Buren, and James Buchanan's First Ladies, but not to Chester A. Arthur's First Lady coin, which depicts suffragette Alice Paul.
one_line: Describes the U.S. Mint's 2007 First Spouse gold coin series and how it depicts presidents served without a spouse.
key_facts: In 2007, the United States Mint began releasing a set of half-ounce $10 gold coins under the First Spouse Program.
The First Spouse Program coins have engravings of portraits of the First Ladies on the obverse.
When a President served without a spouse, a gold coin was issued with an obverse image emblematic of Liberty as depicted on a circulating coin of that era.
For presidents served without a spouse, the coin's reverse image is emblematic of themes of that President's life.
The coin rule for presidents without a spouse applies to the coins for Thomas Jefferson, Andrew Jackson, Martin Van Buren, and James Buchanan's First Ladies.
The coin for Chester A. Arthur's First Lady does not follow the no-spouse design rule.
Chester A. Arthur's First Lady coin instead depicts suffragette Alice Paul.
